methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $9M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Infinite Machine is a seed-stage transportation company founded by Joseph Cohen and Eddie Cohen that has raised $9.3M to date. The transportation sector comp universe includes six private peers—Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Navier, and EarthGrid among them—but no public comparables. No tightly filtered peer set exists at the same stage and valuation tier with sufficient density (need ≥3) to support a peer-median approach.

Valuation analysis applies stage-progression methodology, the sole applicable triangulation method given data constraints. Using total capital raised ($9.3M) as a base proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression yields $23.3M. This reflects the expected value creation between seed and Series A milestones absent company-specific performance metrics or market comparables.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $20M to $27M, with a median of $23M. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-set peer benchmarking, reliance on a single methodological input, and lack of disclosed operational or financial metrics. Materiality of valuation drivers—customer traction, product development velocity, and capital efficiency relative to sector peers—cannot be assessed from available data. A peer-median cross-check would materially strengthen conviction once comparable seed or early-Series A transactions in transportation emerge.
